clue.text: Nobleman upset due to being excluded from activity

parts.note: a count is a continental nobleman

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the next words are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An aristocrat, overturned for some reason, finds himself shut out of what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobleman upset' tempts you to scramble the title itself, but 'upset' works only on the two words after it, giving EDOUT; a boxer floored for ten is the image behind the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer or player is counted out when declared no longer part of the contest, hence excluded.

clue.text: Pirates from whom may be heard rude affectation

indicators.note: may be heard says the words are taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: rude means coarse, and an affectation is putting on airs, giving coarse airs

explanation.surface: A question of which buccaneers one might hear vulgar posturing from.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'coarse airs' (rude affectation) gives the word for Barbary pirates.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsairs were privateers and raiders of the Mediterranean, a literary word for pirates.

clue.text: University head gathers 500 for briefing

indicators.note: gathers means the head takes in the number, which sits inside it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A college principal collects a large sum ahead of giving a briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathers' puts D inside PATE, after U.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is a report bringing someone up to date, much like a briefing.

clue.text: Chariot overturning in the land of Spartacus

indicators.note: in says the upturned vehicle goes inside the following word
overturning means the vehicle is turned upside down, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a chariot is a kind of car, a wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: A chariot crashes over in the homeland of the famous rebel gladiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' flips the vehicle and 'in' sets it inside the article. Spartacus, leader of the slave revolt against Rome, was a Thracian.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace, an ancient region of the Balkans, was where Spartacus came from.

clue.text: Princess meeting poet and pharmacist

parts.note: Di is Diana, Princess of Wales
Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: A royal is introduced to a poet and to a chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser makes up and hands out medicines, as a pharmacist does.

clue.text: Huge number sing by way of conveying love

parts.note: to trill is to sing with a warbling quaver

indicators.note: conveying means carrying, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: in can mean by way of or through, as in paying in cash
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An instruction to sing as a means of carrying affection, ending in a huge figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveying' makes ION, the zero-shaped love carried within the little word for by way of.
explanation.definitionFit: A trillion, a million million, is a vast number and stands for any enormous quantity.

clue.text: Some earl or duke? Possibly

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a certain earl or duke is the man in question.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'Possibly' alone as the definition, which cannot mean the answer; the whole clue defines it, with 'Possibly' marking that earls and dukes are examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls and dukes are peers, each addressed or described as a member of the nobility, so either is possibly this title.

clue.text: Freedom from restraint that is minimal in Quito

definitions.meaning: scope or leeway to act as one chooses
Quito, capital of Ecuador, lies almost on the equator, where the angular distance north or south is close to zero

explanation.surface: Liberty that Ecuador's capital supposedly has very little of.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both leeway and the angular distance from the equator, near zero at Quito.

clue.text: Old fellow in revolt is to become a Catholic

indicators.note: in says the old fellow sits inside the word for revolt

parts.note: to revolt is to rise up
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An elderly man in rebellion decides to convert to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places OMAN inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To Romanise is to convert or bring under Roman Catholic influence, so to turn Catholic.

clue.text: Engineers getting caught, stuck in rubbish — we bring relief

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army

indicators.note: stuck in says the letter is lodged inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: dross is waste or rubbish
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Army engineers are caught and trapped in debris, before the rescuers arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' lodges the cricket letter in the waste; the definition is the organisation speaking for itself in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanitarian organisation speaks for itself here: its whole work is bringing aid and relief.

clue.text: Cosy at home, confronting the enemy

parts.note: someone at home is in
time is called the enemy, as in the saying 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: Staying in to face up to a foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronting' just sets the two pieces side by side; 'the enemy' for TIME is an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Intime is a French borrowing meaning intimate, snug and comfortable.

clue.text: Written pieces, small bits with no heading

indicators.note: with no heading says the first letter is removed, the word losing its head

parts.note: particles are tiny bits

explanation.surface: Short newspaper items and fragments lacking titles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no heading' drops the P from PARTICLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles are pieces of writing in a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Prayer in Latin translated by unknown character

indicators.note: translated suggests a change of form, so the letters of Latin are reworked

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic letters for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A Latin prayer put into another language by a mysterious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' reorders the language's name, and the unknown from algebra completes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a set form of prayer with petitions and responses.

clue.text: Thus house has no use in one part of London

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: has no says the following word is taken out of the one before

explanation.surface: A building that, it turns out, is useless in a certain district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' strips USE from HOUSE, leaving HO. Soho is a West End entertainment district.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of central London's West End.

clue.text: US author may, from what we hear?

indicators.note: from what we hear says the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: may is the blossom of a thorn tree, another name for the tree itself

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an American writer is permitted, going by rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' looks like a verb, but it is the hedge blossom; Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was a nineteenth-century American novelist.

clue.text: Imagine meal mostly containing fat?

indicators.note: containing says the shortened meal holds the next piece inside it
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
OS, outsize, is the clothing label for a large size, hence fat, with a question mark

explanation.surface: Picture a dinner made largely of grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks the evening meal by its last letter; 'containing' takes in the clothing-size label for outsize, which the question mark flags as only an example of fat.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or imagine something to be so.

clue.text: Maybe Oxford poetry is all there is

parts.note: Oxford is an example of a university, a uni
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Perhaps a famous university's poetry is the whole of existence.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the totality of everything that exists.

clue.text: Historical leader of independence, guerrilla in imitation of others

parts.note: something historical is in the past

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: An old freedom-fighter's guerrilla tactics copied from others.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work deliberately imitating the style of another artist or period.

clue.text: Sign of injury that is seen on street causing most dismay

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a wound
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A wound visible in the road is the most alarming sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scariest is the most frightening, causing the greatest alarm.

clue.text: Infuriated and enraged, going berserk

indicators.note: going berserk means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone livid and furious, losing all control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going berserk' rearranges ENRAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Angered is a straight synonym of infuriated, both meaning made very cross.

clue.text: Not bad, we may become pessimistic

indicators.note: may become says the letters could be turned into something else

explanation.surface: We are doing all right but might turn gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may become' rearranges NOTBADWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat describes a gloomy or negative outlook, so pessimistic.

clue.text: Brag as one involved in murder?

definitions.meaning: a murder is the collective noun for a flock of these black birds, so each one is part of a murder

explanation.surface: Boasting like someone mixed up in a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast, and a crow is the bird that gathers in a murder.

clue.text: Little woman coming to the Spanish house of prayer

parts.note: Beth is one of the March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A small lady arrives at a Spanish chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bethel is a chapel, especially a Nonconformist one, from the Hebrew for house of God.

clue.text: Like a racket that's hurt, ear finally having to be covered

indicators.note: having to be covered says the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: stung means hurt

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A wounded tennis bat, with an ear that needs bandaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to be covered' puts R inside STUNG; a tennis racket is strung with gut or nylon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis or squash racket is strung, its face filled with tensioned strings.

clue.text: Divine manifestation of a king at the rear of a tank?

indicators.note: at the rear of says the king comes after the tank

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch perched on the back of an armoured vehicle as a god in earthly form.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'tank' looks military but is a vat; A R goes after A VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief an avatar is a deity's incarnation on earth.

clue.text: Earth disturbed by number seen as menace

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: The planet unsettled by a figure regarded as a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' scrambles the planet's name to give THREA; 'seen as' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace is to threaten, to hold out the prospect of harm.

clue.text: Men only half clever engaging a wise fellow

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the pieces before enclose the next letter

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, ordinary men

indicators.note: only half means just the first half of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Soldiers only half bright taking on a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' is other ranks, not males; 'only half' keeps the front three letters of the adjective, and 'engaging' sets A between the soldiers and that half.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person of great wisdom whose pronouncements are trusted, a sage.

clue.text: Cinema must throw a shouter out

indicators.note: out, after throw, means flung aside into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A picture house has to eject a noisy patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw ... out' rearranges A SHOUTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An art house is a cinema showing independent or foreign films.

clue.text: Expanse of water providing a bit of summer entertainment

indicators.note: a bit of says the answer is a small part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lake that offers some fun during summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' points to letters inside SUMMER ENTERTAINMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake or pond, a broad stretch of still water.

clue.text: Adopt a series of steps to disappear quickly

parts.note: to adopt is to take on
a flight is a series of stairs

explanation.surface: Take up a staircase to vanish fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To take flight is to flee, leaving in a hurry.
